proposal: SHIP demos/routing-backtest (jev-route-backtest) as the lane's negative-result instrument: 'prove routing does not pay on YOUR logs before building a router.' Nothing to build — package with bin/backtest.mjs, install.sh, fixtures, tests exists. Missing piece is one stranger-facing verdict line (0.0447% on our turns, as_of date, do-not-build-router), not code.
runner_up: compaction/ omp-compact-replay harness (proven adapter + live replay) — second because the interesting half needs a Jev key; backtest needs nothing but logs.
verification: ran live this unit: one command, 0.14s, offline, no key, receipted JSON with denominator + failures counter. Bare-invocation arg errors print usage then a TypeError stack (UX wart, not capability gap — noted, not blocking).
why_this_outranks_audits: Per tick §2: a runnable script a non-lane reader consumes outranks every audit. This is the only lane artifact that is installable, offline, keyless, proven, and answers a question outsiders actually ask. Its verdict (do not build) is the ruling's most transferable sentence in executable form.
